items.title: Good Alienation
items.description:
This is the third in a series of responses to Sean Tatol’s issue 37 essay “After the Post-Avant-Garde: How to return to art history.” 
 The post  Good Alienation  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: JD Agonistes
items.description:
Opportunism is the byword for any politician, really, and it is understandable why it might be particularly tempting to employ in Vance’s case. 
 The post  JD Agonistes  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: Getting Good
items.description:
On a dark, gray day in October 2025, the first dozen attendees of the Effective Altruism Global conference make their way to the Sheraton Hotel just north of Times Square in New York City. 
 The post  Getting Good  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: Mommy Magic Show
items.description:
Before Theranos is called Theranos, reports John Carreyrou, it is called Real-Time Cures, and early employees receive paychecks upon which there has been a misprint: their checks call their place of employment “Real-Time Curses.” 
 The post  Mommy Magic Show  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: The Part About the Machines
items.description:
The news has already traveled the world, but for those who haven’t yet heard: three weeks ago, El País published an article declaring that the award-winning novel Donde el agua trabaja, by Peruvian writer David Silva Rojas, was, according to Pangram, 99 percent AI-generated. 
 The post  The Part About the Machines  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: Rejecting Enlightenment
items.description:
“I felt the need to tell my story, and to do so in public, where I’m held accountable by the moral gaze of another person—but at the same time not to reduce it, or simplify it.” 
 The post  Rejecting Enlightenment  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: Flowers for Frank
items.description:
The End of History and the Last Man  is famously talked about more than it is read; as a teenager, however, I did not know this, so after seeing it referenced on multiple blogs, I assumed I had to trudge through the thing. 
 The post  Flowers for Frank  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: After the Sublime
items.description:
The problem with  Backrooms —like much of the online content that inspired it—is less that it relies too much on vibe and more that it fails to understand what makes that vibe interesting in the first place. 
 The post  After the Sublime  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: The Perfect Game
items.description:
It went on long enough that the crowd curdled and its cheers turned sarcastic. 
 The post  The Perfect Game  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .
